target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: security: gateway public network hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive security hardening for OpenClaw Gateway when exposed to public networks (e.g. `https://openclaw.allegro.earth/`). The existing security mechanisms (non-loopback auth enforcement, auth rate limiting, CORS checks) leave gaps that this PR addresses:

- **IP access control** (allowlist/blocklist with CIDR support) — enforced on both HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades, loopback always allowed, blocklist takes priority
- **Password/token strength validation** — CRITICAL startup warnings when network-exposed with short tokens (<32 chars) or weak passwords (<12 chars, all-digit/all-letter patterns)
- **TLS enforcement check** — CRITICAL startup warning when network-exposed without TLS and no `terminatedUpstream` declaration
- **Per-IP request rate limiting** — sliding window (default 120 req/min/IP), loopback exempt by default, returns 429 with Retry-After
- **Auth audit logging** — JSONL to `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-auth.jsonl` with file rotation, records `auth_failure`, `auth_success`, `rate_limited`, `ip_blocked` events
- **Auto HSTS** — `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` set automatically when TLS is enabled
- **Eliminate silent 0.0.0.0 fallback** — `loopback`, `tailnet`, and `custom` bind modes now throw clear errors instead of silently falling back to all-interfaces
- **New security audit checks** — `gateway.no_tls_network_exposed` (critical), `gateway.password_too_short` (critical), `gateway.password_weak_pattern` (warn), `gateway.no_request_rate_limit` (warn), `gateway.auto_bind_fallback` (warn)
- **Enhanced `doctor` warnings** — TLS, password strength, token length, request rate limit checks for network-exposed gateways

### Config additions (`gateway.*`)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ipAllowlist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP allowlist (loopback always allowed) |
| `ipBlocklist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP blocklist (checked before allowlist) |
| `requestRateLimit.maxRequests` | `number` | 120 | Max requests per IP per window |
| `requestRateLimit.windowMs` | `number` | 60000 | Sliding window duration (ms) |
| `requestRateLimit.exemptLoopback` | `boolean` | true | Skip rate limiting for localhost |
| `tls.terminatedUpstream` | `boolean` | false | Declare TLS terminated by reverse proxy |

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — type check passes
- [x] New unit tests: `ip-access-control.test.ts` (9 tests), `request-rate-limit.test.ts` (7 tests), `auth-audit-log.test.ts` (4 tests), `credential-strength.test.ts` (9 tests)
- [x] Existing tests updated and passing: `server-runtime-config.test.ts`, `doctor-security.test.ts`, `net.test.ts`, `auth.test.ts`, `audit.test.ts` — 245 tests total
- [ ] Manual: start gateway with `bind=lan` and verify startup warnings
- [ ] Manual: test IP blocklist returns 403
- [ ] Manual: test request rate limit returns 429

target.title: fix: honor configured default agent across main paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining hardcoded `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID = "main"` assumptions called out in #90573 for deployments whose configured default agent is not `main`.

PR #30654 fixed the main session-key write paths, but #90573 identified follow-on paths that still synthesized `agents/main/*`, `agent:main:*`, or phantom `main` audit scopes even when config declares a different default agent such as `nova`.

This PR uses the existing `agents.list[].default` / first-agent behavior. It intentionally does **not** add a new `agents.defaultAgentId` config key or `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current behavior makes non-`main` default-agent deployments inconsistent: some surfaces honor the configured default agent, while others silently route storage, session keys, setup directories, or audit reporting through `main`. That creates broken paths and confusing phantom state for multi-agent installs.

## User Impact

Deployments whose configured default agent is not `main` can keep using their chosen default agent without residual `main` paths leaking into session initialization, auth/model storage scans, setup transcript directories, or exec-scope audit output.

## Changes

- Key new explicit `sessionId` sessions to the resolved store/default agent instead of literal `main`.
- Thread the resolved agent id into auto-reply session initialization.
- Resolve default auth/model storage scan paths from the configured default agent directory.
- Stop security audit exec-scope reporting from injecting a phantom `main` default when another agent is configured as default.
- Avoid inferring a delivery channel from one-segment agent main-session keys when the agent id happens to match a channel name.
- Let setup create the configured default agent's transcript directory instead of `agents/main/sessions` when config is available.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Compatibility:** no schema/env surface added; legacy `main` aliases are still recognized where they already were.
- **Auth-provider:** storage discovery still includes existing directories under state plus configured agent dirs; this only replaces the synthetic default path.
- **Session-state:** new explicit sessions use the same effective default agent that owns the selected store; existing persisted keys are not migrated here.

## Evidence

Current head: `8bbd81367e8807a741314b9a91cfb99d24b4586e`.
Current base: `6db0506474ceb10c64ea3b5f64e29772fb04280e`.

### Current-head runtime proof

```json
    "isDefault": false,
    "agentDir": "<home>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent",
    "workspace": "<home>/.openclaw/workspace-main"

    "id": "ops",
    "isDefault": true,
    "agentDir": "<home>/.openclaw/agents/ops/agent",
    "workspace": "<home>/.openclaw/workspace"
  }
]
```

Direct runtime proof with configured agents `utility` and default `ops`, plus an existing on-disk `agents/main/agent` store, shows the new default surfaces consistently use `ops` while still discovering the old `main` store:

```json

  "defaultAgentId": "ops",
  "defaultAgentDir": "<state>/agents/ops/agent",
  "sessionKey": "agent:ops:main",
  "sessionStorePath": "<state>/agents/ops/sessions/sessions.json",
  "transcriptDir": "<state>/agents/ops/sessions",
  "authStoreAgentDirs": [
```

That covers the requested proof surfaces: session key/store path, setup transcript path, auth/model scan discovery, audit output, and explicit preservation/discovery of an existing `agents/main` store without treating `main` as the configured default.

target.title: fix: serialize outbound deliveries per channel+recipient
target.body:
## Summary

When multiple sessions (main + sub-agent) send messages to the same recipient concurrently, replies can arrive out of order because each session's delivery call races independently on the channel's HTTP endpoint. Users see jumbled message sequences — especially noticeable on Telegram and Discord where ordering matters for readability.

**Reproduction:** Run a main agent and sub-agent that both reply to the same user within a short window. Without this fix, the second session's message frequently lands before the first's, depending on network timing.

**Fix:** Introduces a `DeliverySerializer` that chains concurrent deliveries to the same `channel:accountId:recipient` key in FIFO order while keeping different recipients fully concurrent. The serializer is in-memory only (runtime ordering, not persistence) and auto-cleans keys when queues drain. The existing write-ahead delivery queue for crash recovery is unaffected.

A follow-up commit wraps `fn()` in `Promise.resolve().then()` so a synchronous throw is converted to a rejection rather than hanging the result promise forever (addresses review feedback).

Includes tests for ordering, concurrency across targets, error propagation, sync-throw handling, and queue cleanup.

Rebased to 2026.3.13.

---

## Real behavior proof — Telegram, live session (2026-05-22)

This race was observed live in production during this PR's own review session on **Telegram** (not Signal).

**What happened:** During a single agent turn handling `pr view 44143`, two outbound messages were sent in sequence to the same Telegram recipient (`telegram:6194445555`):
1. A long ClawSweeper analysis dump (~4KB)
2. A summary message referencing and synthesizing that analysis

**Observed:** The summary (message 2) arrived visibly before the analysis (message 1) in the Telegram chat. The recipient had to read the synthesis before the content it was synthesizing — the exact inversion this PR fixes.

**Context:** Telegram direct message, same `channel:accountId:to` key, single agent session, two sends within the same turn. No sub-agent involved — the race can happen within a single session turn when one send is large enough to lose the HTTP timing race against a smaller follow-up send.

**Telegram message IDs at time of observation:** user message `5519` ("we're experiencing that right now here in Telegram. Look at your last 3 messages"), preceded by the two inverted agent messages. Timestamp: 2026-05-22 ~15:00 EDT.

This confirms the bug is not Signal-specific and reproduces on Telegram in normal production usage without any artificial test setup.

target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

Real environment tested: macOS 26.2 on Apple Silicon, Node 24.13.0, pnpm 11.2.2, against the fork branch tip at commit `5cdaf8e774`. A reproduction harness at the repo root (`repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`, not committed) imports the real `src/agents/workspace.ts` from this branch and invokes `resolveBootstrapTier` and `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` against an explicit `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` containing both root-loaded files and hook-loaded extras whose basenames collide with the root allowlist.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `git checkout 5cdaf8e774` (this PR's head)
2. `pnpm install --prefer-offline --frozen-lockfile`
3. Author the reproduction harness at the repo root, importing `./src/agents/workspace.js` and calling the exported functions directly with a `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` shaped like a real workspace (root files + two hook-sourced `packages/*/AGENTS.md` entries).
4. `node ./node_modules/.bin/tsx repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`

Evidence after fix:

Terminal capture, run live against commit `5cdaf8e774`:

```text

===== resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride) =====
  (no sessionKey)  default=standard   override=minimal→minimal   override=standard→standard   override=full→full
  main session      default=standard   override=minimal→minimal   override=standard→standard   override=full→full
  subagent session  default=minimal   override=minimal→minimal   override=standard→standard   override=full→full
  cron session      default=minimal   override=minimal→minimal   override=standard→standard   override=full→full

===== filterBootstrapFilesForSession — DEFAULTS (no tierOverride) =====
(no sessionKey), no override  →  10 file(s):
    - /tmp/proof-workspace/AGENTS.md  [root]
    - /tmp/proof-workspace/TOOLS.md  [root]
    - /tmp/proof-workspace/SOUL.md  [root]
```

## Summary

- Add `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` to control which agents a specific agent may contact via session tools (`sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `session_status`)
- When unset, the agent falls back to the global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` list; when set to explicit IDs, only those targets are reachable; `[]` isolates the agent from all cross-agent access
- The global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` continues to act as a participation gate (both requester and target must match it) before per-agent outbound rules are evaluated
- Outbound-only semantics: only the requester's override is checked, not the target's
- Replace `matchesAllow` with `matchesGlobalParticipation` and add `evaluateAccess()` returning a structured `AgentToAgentDenyReason` so all call sites produce context-aware error messages via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`
- Scrub deleted agent references from per-agent outbound allowlists in `pruneAgentConfig()`

### Example config (hub-spoke pattern)

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "david",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["*"] } } },
      { "id": "spoke",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } },
      { "id": "kelly",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } }
    ]
  }
}
```

target.title: fix(skills): list omitted skill names when prompt is truncated
target.body:
## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DuckDuckGo web search results could expose DuckDuckGo-relative redirect paths such as /l/?uddg=... instead of the real destination URL when the HTML result page uses relative tracking links.

## Why This Change Was Made

The DuckDuckGo provider now resolves result hrefs against the DuckDuckGo origin before reading the existing uddg redirect parameter. This keeps direct result URLs and existing absolute/protocol-relative redirect handling unchanged while covering the same owner-local parsing invariant for root-relative redirect links.

## User Impact

Users choosing DuckDuckGo as their web search provider now receive usable destination URLs for relative redirect results instead of local DuckDuckGo tracking paths.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: DuckDuckGo result URL parsing decodes direct URLs, absolute/protocol-relative redirect URLs, and root-relative /l/?uddg=... redirect URLs, including through parsed HTML search results.
- Preserved real DuckDuckGo root-relative proof: a public Stack Overflow report for `requests.get('http://duckduckgo.com/html/?q=hello')` records a DuckDuckGo HTML result href as `/l/?kh=-1&uddg=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.example.com`, and the accepted answer parses the same root-relative href shape by reading the `uddg` destination parameter: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52801138/scraping-site-returns-different-href-for-a-link

Feature Request: Dynamic/Contextual Ack Reactions

Currently, OpenClaw uses a single fixed emoji for ackReaction (default 👀) to acknowledge messages before processing. This works but feels repetitive and robotic in group chats.

Proposal:
Allow the agent to choose contextually appropriate reactions based on message content/tone, either:
From a configured array of emojis (ackReactions: ["👀", "👍", "🤔", "✅"] - agent picks)
Or let the agent dynamically decide per-message (like it does with tool calls)

Use Case:
In group chats, varied reactions feel more natural and human-like. "👀" for everything gets stale. A thinking emoji (🤔) for complex questions, thumbs up (👍) for acknowledgments, checkmark (✅) for tasks, etc. makes the bot feel less mechanical.

Current Workaround:
Manually calling message tool with action=react on every message - adds latency and API calls.

Preferred:
Native support in the channel config or agent behavior layer.

target.title: fix(moonshot): forward abort signal through Kimi web search provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users cancelling an agent run while a Kimi (Moonshot) `web_search` request was pending would leave that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reached the generic web-search runtime, but the Kimi provider discarded the execution context, so the request could remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

The Kimi tool accepted only `args` and dropped the tool execution context — `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` had no `opts` parameter and `createTool` ignored `context`. The downstream `runKimiSearch` already accepted a `signal` field but the caller never passed one in, so the signal died at the provider boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause fix across the existing cancellation boundaries: the Kimi tool now accepts the execution context and passes its `AbortSignal` through `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` → `runKimiSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`.

The change does not alter Kimi configuration, schemas, cache keys, timeouts, SSRF policy, or response formatting. Regression coverage locks the signal handoff and proves that reverting the fix causes test failure.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Kimi web search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool entry | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 63 | `execute: async (args, context)` accepts context |
| Signal pass | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 66 | `{ signal: context?.signal }` |
| Tool exec | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 349 | `opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }` |
| Run search | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 401 | `signal: opts?.signal` |
| Search client | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 234 | `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal: params.signal })` |
| SSRF guard | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })` |
| Timeout | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` |
| Native | `fetch()` | — | Native `AbortSignal` support |

### Real behavior proof — pre-aborted signal through full provider chain

```
[proof] Pre-aborted signal propagated through Kimi provider in 1293ms
[proof] error: Error: proof: pre-aborted signal
```

- Signal flows from provider.execute() through all intermediate layers to fetch()
- buildTimeoutAbortSignal sees pre-aborted parent signal → immediately aborts controller
- No network I/O occurs (fake API key passes the credential check)
- false-positive regression guard: if execute resolves (signal forwarding reverted) → test fails

### Real behavior proof — in-flight cancel through real Kimi API

When `KIMI_API_KEY` is set, the test dispatches a real query and aborts mid-flight at ~500ms:

```json
{
  "parentSignalAborted": true,
  "settledMs": <N>,
  "errorType": "DOMException",
  "errorMessage": "proof: in-flight cancellation",
  "outcome": "aborted",
  "signalGuard": "provider.execute → runKimiSearch → withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint → fetch()"
}
```

### Real behavior proof — stalled-server through guarded-fetch stack

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 110ms through guarded-fetch stack
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
```

(withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint shares identical fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch() path)

### Regression test — signal reaches fetch (control-red verifiable)

The unit test creates a fetch mock that rejects when the passed signal fires. The test:
1. Starts a search with an `AbortController`
2. Waits for fetch() to be called
3. Aborts the controller mid-flight
4. Asserts the search rejects
5. Asserts the signal passed to fetch is defined and aborted

**Control-red**: reverting `signal: context?.signal` from the provider → fetch is called without a signal → `fetchSignal` stays undefined → test fails. This was NOT true in R2 where the test only checked `fetchMock.toHaveBeenCalled()` (passes even with reverted fix).

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
 ✓ 19/19 passed (2 test files)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
✓ clean (exit 0)
```

### tsgo

```
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
✓ exit 0, no errors
```

### Control-red

| Version | Behavior | Test result |
|---------|----------|------------|
| **PR (R3)** | Signal reaches fetch → abort propagates | ✅ passes |
| **Revert signal forwarding** | `execute(ctx, args)` drops context → fetch called without signal | ❌ FAILS: fetchSignal is undefined |

Revert diff (the exact lines removed to test):
```diff
- execute: async (args, context) => {
-   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args, { signal: context?.signal });
+ execute: async (args) => {
+   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args);
```

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Recovery is now bounded on three axes flagged in review:

- **Thread response size.** `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` requests only the newest `historyLimit + 1` posts via `?perPage=<limit>&direction=up`, then restores ascending chronological order. `GET /posts/{id}/thread` returns the entire thread at the Mattermost default (`perPage=0`), so an unbounded thread would otherwise allocate and parse on the inbound path. The endpoint reads camelCase `perPage` (not `per_page`), so the limit is actually applied.
- **Marker lifecycle.** Backfill tracking uses one marker per thread history key (`Map<historyKey, sessionId>`) instead of a process-lifetime `Set` of `historyKey:session` compound keys. A plugin-local 1000-key LRU cap (`evictOldThreadBackfillMarkers`, matching the `channelHistories` window size) keeps the marker map from outgrowing the history window it accompanies; the cap stays in the plugin rather than touching core history internals. An evicted thread simply re-backfills on its next cold inbound turn. The stored session id is read only after the admission gates, so dropped pre-admission posts never touch the session store.
- **Concurrent cold turns.** Under the default zero-debounce config, two first cold-thread messages can overlap on the awaited thread-history fetch. The first turn sets the completed-attempt marker and publishes a per-history-key in-flight promise; an overlapping same-session turn now awaits that one bounded fetch instead of seeing the marker and skipping into a context-free reply. The in-flight handle is cleared once the fetch settles, so afterward the marker alone governs the intentional one-attempt-per-session no-retry.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests, unbounded thread fetches, or unbounded per-session marker growth on long-lived monitors. Concurrent first cold-thread messages under zero-debounce no longer race into a context-free reply.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: **3 files, 115 passed**. Covers stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, dropped pre-admission posts, adopt-pending-marker without blocking later rotation, the initially-missing session entry path, marker-map eviction, and the new concurrent-turn deferred-fetch case.
- `oxlint` (repo binary) on the changed prod + test files: **passed**. `tsgo --noEmit -p extensions/mattermost/tsconfig.json`: **passed**.
- Bounded fetch asserted (`client.test.ts`): a limited call issues `?perPage=2&direction=up` and re-sorts ascending so callers still build history oldest-first.
- Bounded marker asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): the backfill requests `historyLimit + 1`, `threadBackfillMarkers.get(historyKey)` carries the current session marker across the rotation / no-refetch / no-retry / adopt paths, and the eviction test drives 1001 distinct threads to prove the marker map stays capped at 1000 (plugin-local LRU), the oldest key is evicted, and an evicted thread with a cold window re-backfills from the server.
- Concurrency asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): with the first cold fetch gated open, an overlapping same-session turn stays pending until that fetch releases, exactly one server fetch runs, both turns observe the recovered window, and the in-flight handle is cleared afterward so the marker governs no-retry.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` (0 behind). The only conflict was two independent `describe` blocks colliding in `client.test.ts` (`createMattermostDirectChannelWithRetry delay cap` from main and `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` from this branch); both were kept. Earlier exact-head repairs remain: the thread query uses Mattermost's documented camelCase `perPage` so the response bound is applied, and the chronological re-sort uses non-mutating `toSorted()` to satisfy the bundled-extension `unicorn/no-array-sort` lint lane.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where backend clients retrying a failed `chat.send` with the same idempotency key could not tell that the Gateway had returned a stored result. A cached retryable error therefore looked fresh and could be resubmitted until the client's retry budget was exhausted.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the broad metadata forwarding proposed in #98206 with a narrow negotiated contract:

- `response-replay` is an explicit client capability.
- The only wire metadata is the closed JSON shape `{ replayed: true }`.
- Core Gateway handlers use an internal responder with a dedicated wire-metadata argument.
- Plugin handlers retain the existing four-argument responder contract; the plugin adapter strips any attempted fifth argument.
- Clients without the capability receive the unchanged strict response envelope.
- The official TypeScript Gateway client advertises the capability and exposes `GatewayClientRequestError.replayed`, providing an in-tree consumer.

`runId`, diagnostic `error`/`channel` values, and plugin metadata are never copied into the response metadata object.

## User Impact

Retrying clients can stop resubmitting the same idempotency key after the Gateway returns a stored retryable error. Existing clients and native apps that do not advertise `response-replay` see no new response-frame fields.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `6f9a607b90393b14d769ec4696b99a6dc057498f`; current PR head is `4d4b07963d666bc2ac3ac5665b72998b3ab109da`.
- Exact-head loopback WebSocket proof passed through the current `message-handler.ts` and official `GatewayClient`:
  - legacy `caps: []` received the unchanged response with no `meta`;
  - the official client advertised `response-replay`, received only `meta: { replayed: true }`, and raised `GatewayClientRequestError` with `gatewayCode: "UNAVAILABLE"`, `retryable: true`, and `replayed: true`;
  - log-only sentinels were absent from both wire responses.
- Plugin ownership regression passed: a plugin's attempted fifth responder argument is removed before the core responder is called.
- Full plugin loader suite passed: 175/175.
- Focused protocol, client, Gateway handler, and cached-chat suites passed: 247/247 across 9 test files.
- Plugin SDK surface check passed with no forbidden package exports.
- Full TypeScript project graph passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b tsconfig.projects.json`.
- Protocol and Swift models remain aligned; `ResponseFrame.meta` is optional and legacy clients retain the strict old envelope.

The earlier live WebSocket capture in #98206 establishes the original dropped-metadata behavior. The current exact-head proof separately verifies the negotiated compatibility, core-only producer boundary, and official-client behavior introduced by this PR.

target.title: fix(channels): retain draft preview id after failed delete for retry (#104865)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord partial streaming forgets the preview message ID after a cleanup DELETE failure, leaving a stale preview beside the fresh final reply with no way to retry the cleanup.

Closes #104865.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clearFinalizableDraftMessage` called `takeMessageIdAfterStop`, which cleared the stored preview ID **before** attempting the DELETE call. If the DELETE failed (e.g., Discord returns HTTP 500), the ID was already forgotten, so no later cleanup call could retry it.

This change moves the ID clear to **after** a successful DELETE, with a compare-and-clear guard: the ID is only cleared if the stored ID still matches the one that was just deleted, preventing accidental erasure of a newer preview that replaced it while the DELETE was in flight.

## User Impact

Discord users with partial streaming enabled: a transient DELETE failure no longer leaves an unrecoverable stale preview. The preview ID survives the failed cleanup and can be retried by a subsequent cleanup call. The existing `onDeleteSuccess` callback and successful cleanup behavior are unchanged.

Mattermost users also benefit from the same compare-and-clear safety since they share this shared helper.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/channels/draft-stream-controls.test.ts` — **8/8 passed** (7 existing + 1 new)
  - New: `clearFinalizableDraftMessage retains the id after a failed delete for retry` — proves ID survives first failed DELETE and clears after second successful DELETE
  - All existing tests pass unchanged

target.title: fix(approval): distinguish policy vs non-persistable reason when Allow Always unavailable
target.body:
Fixes #97069.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running commands with shell redirection (e.g. `openclaw --version 2>&1`) would see "The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable" — even when their effective policy is `ask=on-miss`. All nine approval prompt renderers (reply, forwarder, agent-facing, Control UI, reaction, embedded handler, Telegram handler, Telegram forwarding, and gateway API) blamed the policy instead of the real cause: the command is non-persistable and cannot be saved as an allow-always rule.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` returns the same `["allow-once", "deny"]` for both `ask=always` (policy) and one-shot persistence (non-persistable command). Downstream renderers had no way to distinguish the two cases.

Rather than introducing a new typed protocol field (which previous attempts attempted across 65+ files), we thread the existing `ask` field — already present in the request payload, approval view, and gateway pipeline — through the approval-pending data pipeline so renderers can branch on it. Approval policy logic is unchanged.

The `node` host path uses `approvalDecisionAsk` (`maxAsk(hostAsk, nodeAsk)`) to keep the reasoning consistent with `allowedDecisions` computation even when the node policy is stricter than the host policy.

## User Impact

Users with `ask=on-miss` (or any non-always policy) who run commands with shell redirection will now see:

> Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

Instead of the misleading policy message. Users with `ask=always` see the same policy message as before. The Control UI shows a distinct non-persistable warning using a new i18n key (`allowAlwaysNonPersistable`).

| `ask` input | Message shown |
|---|---|
| `"always"` | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" |
| `"on-miss"` (one-shot) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" |
| `"off"` (shell redirect) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" |
| absent / null | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (safe default) |

## Evidence

**18 files, +109/−23 lines.** Core logic is 52 lines; tests add 57 lines.

**Renderers fixed (all 9):** reply, forwarder, agent-facing, Control UI, reaction, embedded handler, Telegram handler, Telegram forwarding, gateway API error message.

**Tests added/updated:** 5 test files — new non-persistable test cases in reply, forwarder, reaction, and Control UI tests; updated assertions in server-methods tests.

**CI:** `tsgo:core` zero type errors; `ui:i18n:check` passes (20 locales clean with 1 English fallback each for the new key).

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
3. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and require provider attribution from wrapper/config output instead of inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it no longer changes `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP calls only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Gateway `/v1/embeddings` and capability-CLI paths call `embed` / `embedBatch` without a signal, so a server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends headers could hang the request forever. Memory/wiki callers already install their own deadlines; this gap is the unsignaled transport path.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `signal` is omitted, pass `timeoutMs: 60_000` into the existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` hang bound (aligned with memory remote query defaults). When a caller already provides a signal, leave that deadline alone so memory search / tool timeouts are not clamped to 30–60s.

No new config surface. Test-only override shortens the floor for hang repros.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding requests (gateway HTTP embeddings, capability CLI) could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Those requests fail with `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` after 60s. Callers that pass `AbortSignal` keep their own budget.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts` (`postEmbeddingRequest`)
- Production caller under test: `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider(...).provider.embed(...)` against a real local `node:http` server that never responds
- Regression: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`
- Sibling cases still green in the same file (UTF-16 error bounds, oversized JSON cancel, auth/config paths)

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |plugins| ... > times out embedding requests that never respond when caller omits signal 59ms
 ✓ |plugins| ... > keeps caller AbortSignal deadlines instead of the no-signal transport floor 201ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.18s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding POSTs no longer hang forever when the upstream accepts the connection but never responds.
- **Canonical reachability path:** gateway `embeddings-http` / capability CLI / direct provider → `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider` → `embed` / `embedBatch` → `postEmbeddingRequest` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ timeoutMs })` when `signal` is absent.
- **Boundary crossed:** Operator/remote OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP → local AbortSignal timeout via guarded fetch.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reuses `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs` / `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`. Does not override caller-owned signals used by memory-core `runEmbeddingOperationWithTimeout`. Does not add config/env.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Node source checkout; production `provider.embed()` against real `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` that reads the body and never writes a response.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash

```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.18s
```

## What Problem This Solves

`openTab` could sticky-adopt a tab whose **final** URL failed browser SSRF policy. Chrome MCP and CDP create-target paths set `runtime.lastTargetId` before `assertBrowserNavigationResultAllowed`. When an allowed request URL redirected to a private endpoint (for example `http://127.0.0.1/...`), `openTab` still rejected — but the blocked target stayed sticky for the next targetless browser action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Align Chrome MCP and CDP create-target adoption with the existing raw `/json/new` contract already documented in the same file: adopt `lastTargetId` only after post-navigation policy passes. Playwright `createPageViaPlaywright` already validates before returning, so it needed no change.

## User Impact

**Before:** A rejected redirect open could still become the implicit target for later snapshot/act calls that omit `targetId`.

**After:** Policy-blocked final URLs do not update `lastTargetId`; the next targetless action keeps the previous sticky target and cannot land on the blocked tab via sticky selection.

Long-running autonomous sessions accumulate message turns indefinitely in `SessionHistorySseState.sentHistory.messages` without any pruning. The in-memory array grows without bound, leading to OOM crashes on constrained hosts.

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/buttons/device directives
target.body:
## What problem this solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]`, `[[buttons:]]`, and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output — common in LLM output — produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects an empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped (message loss).
- **buttons** / **device** → an action whose `label` is empty (also invalid).

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties); agenda/buttons/device didn't.

Fixes #105380

## What changed

`extensions/line/src/reply-payload-transform.ts`: route the agenda, buttons, and device comma-lists through the existing `normalizeStringEntries` helper (same as `[[quick_replies:]]`), instead of three ad-hoc trim/filter pipelines. One canonical normalization path, no drift.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[buttons: Menu \| Choose \| Opt1:d1, Opt2:d2,]]` | 3 actions, 1 empty label | 2 actions, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty action label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda/buttons, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without fix (origin/main parser):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events   → expected '📋 Today (3 events)' to be '📋 Today (2 events)'
 × drops trailing commas in buttons actions  → expected length 2 but got 3
 × drops doubled commas in device controls   → expected [Array(6)] to not include ''
 Tests  3 failed | 12 passed (15)

# with fix:
 Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Typecheck (`tsgo -b tsconfig.extensions.projects.json`) clean.

target.title: fix(usage-bar): bound numeric verb arguments
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep strict integer parsing for usage-template `fixed` and `meter` arguments.
- Preserve the shipped `Number.prototype.toFixed` precision contract at `0..100` instead of narrowing it to `0..20`.
- Keep `meter` width bounded at `1..100` and document both ranges plus the existing built-in footer fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

The first repair correctly rejected partial and excessive numeric tokens, but it also made previously valid `fixed:21` through `fixed:100` templates render empty and silently switch to the built-in footer. Operators also had no public reference for the newly enforced limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fixed` and `meter` share the strict parser but have different resource contracts. `meter` width directly controls loop and output size, so `1..100` remains the bounded range. `fixed` delegates to the shipped Node formatter, whose supported precision is `0..100`; preserving that range avoids an unnecessary compatibility break while still rejecting `101` before `toFixed` is called.

## User Impact

Existing custom templates using `fixed:21..100` continue to render. Malformed, unsafe, negative, scientific, and out-of-range numeric tokens still fail quickly and use the existing built-in footer when the custom result is empty.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** upgrades no longer silently replace valid high-precision custom footers, while billion-cell meter requests remain bounded.
- **What did NOT change:** These surfaces are unchanged and out of scope: usage-template schema, loader/watch behavior, built-in footer format, reply transport, session state, public protocol, and default verb arguments.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #89835, which introduced the native templated usage footer renderer and its numeric verbs.
- **Linked comparison:** closed #105063 only addressed partial parsing and did not own the final range/test/docs fix.
- **Gap this fills:** preserves the formatter-supported compatibility range and publishes the enforced contract.

## Architecture / source-of-truth

- **Canonical reachability path:** operator config input in `messages.usageTemplate` → config schema/type acceptance → `loadUsageBarTemplate` ingestion → `resolveResponseUsageLine` runtime object → `renderUsageBar` / `applyVerb` normalization and validation → custom footer or built-in fallback effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** Operator-authored interpolation tokens cross the template loader into the synchronous agent reply renderer.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** `parseStrictInteger` from `@openclaw/normalization-core` remains the shared strict-token parser; verb-specific ranges remain owned by the usage-bar translator.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical source-of-truth is `translator.ts` for DSL verb semantics and `docs/concepts/usage-tracking.md` for the public operator contract.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** the source invariant was defined too narrowly in the first repair: it treated both numeric verbs as if they shared the same resource ceiling, even though fixed precision is a formatter contract and meter width is an allocation/loop contract.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the canonical translator owner now preserves each consumer's actual invariant before formatting: strict complete integer tokens, fixed precision `0..100`, and meter width `1..100`.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** The author-side blocker is addressed by the compatibility repair, docs, refreshed proof, and verification below.
- **RF-002:** `fixed:21` through `fixed:100` are valid again and no longer trigger built-in fallback.
- **RF-003:** The public usage tracking guide now documents both numeric ranges and fallback behavior.
- **RF-004:** The translator preserves Node's supported fixed precision range `0..100`; `fixed:101` remains rejected.
- **RF-005:** The verb table documents `fixed 0..100`, `meter 1..100`, defaults, strict token semantics, and invalid-render fallback.
- **RF-006:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts` passed all 17 tests.
- **RF-007:** The requested scoped `check:changed` passed conflict, attribution, wildcard-export, duplicate coverage, dependency pin, and touched-file formatting guards. It then stopped only on the global Plugin SDK baseline, which this PR does not touch; no unrelated generated hash was changed. Focused test/format/lint/docs/diff checks are green, and hosted current-head CI remains the final broad check.
- **RF-008:** `git diff --check` passed.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** strict numeric template arguments, fixed precision compatibility, bounded meter width, and built-in fallback through the production footer selection path.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2, current OpenClaw source at commit `e8d17a92f1f4fe88bacd7b5bdcb08635650ba237`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** A bounded TypeScript harness imported production `resolveResponseUsageLine`, supplied inline `messages.usageTemplate` objects, crossed `loadUsageBarTemplate`, contract building, translator verbs, and fallback selection, and wrote evidence only after all assertions passed.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
path=messages.usageTemplate -> loadUsageBarTemplate -> resolveResponseUsageLine -> renderUsageBar/applyVerb -> custom footer or built-in fallback
invalid_case_count=11
fixed:101 => Usage: 100 in / 20 out
fixed:1e2 => Usage: 100 in / 20 out
fixed:2junk => Usage: 100 in / 20 out
fixed:9007199254740992 => Usage: 100 in / 20 out
meter:1000000000 => Usage: 100 in / 20 out
meter:12junk => Usage: 100 in / 20 out
fixed:2 => 100.00
fixed:21 length => 25
fixed:100 length => 104
meter:10 => _____-----
meter:100 length => 100
result=PASS
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Valid fixed precisions 21 and 100 render custom output; fixed 101 and all invalid meter/fixed tokens select the existing built-in footer; valid meter widths 10 and 100 render normally.
- **What was not tested:** A complete provider-backed agent turn was not required because the changed boundary ends inside the deterministic production usage-footer selection function. The actual config loader, usage contract, translator, and fallback consumer were exercised without mocks.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** `fixed:21` and `fixed:100` remain accepted; `fixed:101`, partial, scientific, negative, and unsafe integers remain rejected; `meter:100` remains valid and `meter:101` remains rejected.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** it directly drives the shared numeric verb owner and distinguishes formatter compatibility from meter resource bounds without changing the template format.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

A related open PR / competition scan found no same-contract open replacement. Closed #105063 was reviewed for scope; this existing PR remains the canonical combined strict-parser, bounded-meter, compatible-fixed, tests, docs, and production-proof change.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: compatibility`; availability remains improved by the meter cap.
- **Risk explanation:** the first revision would have invalidated existing `fixed:21..100` templates. This update removes that compatibility regression while retaining strict rejection of malformed and excessive inputs.
- **Why acceptable:** valid shipped formatter behavior is restored, only invalid or resource-excessive tokens fall back, and no API/schema/protocol/default changes are introduced.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High; RED/GREEN compatibility coverage, focused checks, public docs, current-head production-function proof, and explicit broad-check attribution are present.
- **Patch quality notes:** The patch quality warning was checked explicitly: no downstream masking fallback, new parser, schema migration, public surface, lockfile, generated baseline, or unrelated cleanup was added.

## What was not changed

- Usage-template schema and file watcher behavior.
- Built-in footer text and fallback selection semantics.
- Reply delivery, provider usage collection, session state, and protocol.
- Default `fixed:2` and `meter:5` behavior.

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

Restart the gateway to load plugins.

{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],

    "include": [
      "capsule.*",

      "vision_map.describe_workflow",

      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",

    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",

      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs

```


Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
